reason: Driven at 390/768/1152/1279/1280/1440 in chromium, with and without max-width force-removed. The raw numbers check out (rule 20-364 at 390; 96-440 at 768 and 1152; 105.5-449.5 at 1279; exactly 106-450 filling the 344px left column at 1280 and 186-530 at 1440), and deleting max-width really does leave 1280/1440 untouched and does not overflow any column. But the finding is wrong on its central premise and its fix is a regression. (1) The alignment premise is false. It claims .b-who, .b-when, .b-sub, .b-todayLabel and .b-gapNote 'all hold exactly' a right margin the rule misses. Those are text elements: their boxes span the track, their ink does not. At 390 their ink stops at 125.6 / 246.7 / 106.5 / 153.8 / 240.1 - nothing in the identity block has a visible right edge at 370 for the rule to be '6px short of'. A full-element sweep of every painted background and border confirms the only things terminating at 370 are .b-bar's border-bottom (y=143.9), .b-behind's border-top (y=1792) and .b-foot's border-top (y=1954), while the rule sits at y=403 - the nearest comparable hairline is 259px above it with the 79-day counter, the date and 'Wedding day' in between. There is no adjacent edge the eye can compare, so the claimed 'rendering fault' read does not survive being looked at. (2) The premise is false at the wide widths too. .b-gapNote is capped at max-width: 46ch and measures 457.5px, ending at 553.5 inside a 672 track at 768, 553.5 inside 1056 at 1152 and 563 inside 1173.5 at 1279. The identity block already deliberately contains a second element shorter than its track; it is not a right-justified stack, so 'the one object that does not line up' is not accurate. (3) The fix makes the work worse and reverts an adjudicated correction. b.css lines 96-100 carry the reason for the cap in the source: from 701 to 1279 the field is one wide track and the single indigo mark ran the full 1068px of it, 'reading as a divider rather than as today'. Deleting max-width restores precisely that - a 576px, 960px and 1068px solid indigo bar at 768, 1152 and 1279, verified in the strip run. In a strictly three-colour system where ink hairlines at 16% alpha are the structural dividers (.b-bar, .b-behind, .b-foot all use exactly that vocabulary), making the sole accent adopt the same full-track geometry collapses the one distinction that lets it read as a mark rather than as furniture. The finding's largest complaints (616px and 724px short) are requests for exactly that regression. The only defensible residue is 6px on the phone, where the author's stated intent ('a no-op on a phone') is missed because the phone column is 350 not 344; that is invisible in situ, and the finding's fix is not the way to reach it.
